meta.title: Mountain GPX — Automatic waypoints on your GPX track
meta.description: Automatically add waypoints (peaks, passes, mountain huts, water points…) to your hiking or trail running GPX track, from OpenStreetMap data. Enriched GPX and Garmin TCX export. Free, runs 100% in your browser.

about.title: About Mountain GPX
about.p1: Mountain GPX automatically adds waypoints to a hiking, trail running or mountain-bike GPX track: peaks, mountain passes, huts and shelters, springs, fountains and water points, lakes, waterfalls, viewpoints… Points of interest come from OpenStreetMap and are snapped onto your route.
about.p2: Import your GPX, FIT, TCX or KML track (exported from Strava, Komoot, Garmin Connect…), pick the point-of-interest types, then download the enriched track as GPX or TCX (a Garmin course with typed CoursePoints) for your watch or GPS.
about.p3: The tool is free, requires no sign-up and runs entirely in your browser: your file never leaves your device. Installable as an app (PWA), it keeps working offline in the mountains, with a printable roadbook and an elevation profile. An optional hydration plan estimates the water to carry and flags the stretches without a water point.

dropzone.drop: Drop your GPX, FIT, TCX or KML track
dropzone.openTitle: Nothing is sent to a server — everything stays on your device.

th.namedTitle: Include POIs that have a name in OpenStreetMap — the waypoint reuses that name (e.g. “Col de la Vache”).
th.nonameTitle: Also include POIs without a name in OpenStreetMap — a numbered generic name is assigned (e.g. saddle1, spring2).

advanced.customHelp: A single element, in Overpass QL.

hydration.effortHelp: 1 effort-km = 1 km on the flat = 100 m of climb (e.g. 10 km with 600 m of climb = 16 effort-km).
hydration.enable: Show the plan on the profile and the roadbook
hydration.off: Turn the display on to estimate the water to carry and spot the stretches without a water point.
hydration.noteRisk: Fill right up — {km} km with no water point ahead
hydration.sourcesHelp: Taken from the track's waypoints: generate the water points first.
hydration.empty: Load a track to estimate the water to carry.
hydration.alert: {n} stretch(es) longer than your flasks allow. Worst one: {km} km / {time} between {from} and {to} — {missing} short.
hydration.bandTitle: Stretch with no water point: more than your flasks hold

water.zoomIn: Zoom in to load water points

share.title: Share the track and its waypoints by link or GPX file — nothing is sent to a server.
share.linkHelp: The track and its waypoints travel in the link — nothing is sent to a server.
share.fileHelp: Shares the full file — no simplification — through the device share menu.

toast.multiTrack: The file contains {n} tracks: they were joined end to end
toast.selectPoi: Select at least one POI type
toast.partialFail: {n} waypoint(s) — {failed}/{total} section(s) of the route could not be queried, try again
toast.shareCopied: Share link copied to the clipboard
toast.shareCopiedSimplified: Link copied — track simplified to {n} points (of {total}) to fit in the URL

error.shareFailed: Could not create the share link
error.gpxUrlScheme: Only an https:// address can be loaded with #gpx=.
error.gpxUrlCors: Nothing came back from {host}: the host does not allow cross-origin reads (CORS) — the usual cause, and only the host can fix it — or the network is down. This is not a missing file: that comes back as an HTTP 404. GitHub raw and Gists do allow CORS, most track-sharing sites don't — re-host the file there.
error.gpxUrlTimeout: {host} did not answer within {s} s: the download was given up. The host may be down or very slow — try again, or re-host the file.
error.gpxUrlHttp: {host} answered HTTP {status}: the link is broken, or the file is not public. The download itself was not blocked.
error.gpxUrlFormat: The file downloaded from {host} is not a recognizable track (GPX, FIT, TCX or KML) — check that the link points at the file itself and not at a web page.
error.gpxUrlTooBig: The file hosted on {host} is too large to be opened in the browser (limit {max} MB).
error.badFormat: Unsupported format — expected a .gpx, .fit, .tcx or .kml file
error.fileInvalidXml: Invalid file: the XML could not be read.
error.gpxInvalidXml: Invalid GPX file: the XML could not be read.
error.gpxNoPoints: No track (trkpt) or route (rtept) found in the GPX.
error.tcxNoPoints: No trackpoints found in the TCX file.
error.kmlNoPoints: No track found in the KML file.
error.fitNoPoints: No positions found in the FIT file.
error.customQueryInvalid: Invalid custom Overpass query: a single element is expected, e.g. node["tourism"="viewpoint"]
